sources.title: Measured relay resource exhaustion
passages: The author reports a new controlled study on 40 relays using Tor 1.2.3 during November 8–9. Its measurements show a directory-request rate limit refusing about half the requests while admitted directory streams still saturated the measured main threads.
The study does not identify an attacker or establish that all Tor relays are affected.

sources.title: [tor-dev] [Proposal] Fold extra-info fields into router descriptors
passages: I have written a specification proposal to stop publishing separate extra-info documents and to carry their remaining fields in router descriptors instead.
The full text and motivation are in a specification merge request. Comments are welcome.

sources.title: [tor-dev] [RFC] Padding negotiation for onion service circuits
passages: This RFC describes a way for clients and onion services to negotiate circuit padding before any data is sent.

sources.title: [tor-dev] Proposal 901: Relay bandwidth self-reporting limits
passages: Filename: 901-bandwidth-self-reporting-limits.md
Status: Open
This proposal caps the bandwidth a relay may self-report at twice its measured value. Comments are welcome.

sources.title: [tor-dev] New Internet-Draft: draft-example-onion-resolution-00
passages: We have posted draft-example-onion-resolution-00, an Internet-Draft that describes how DNS resolvers should refuse to resolve .onion names.
Comments from Tor developers are welcome on the IETF list or here.

sources.title: [tor-dev] Re: Private address handling
passages: RFC 1918 already lists these address ranges as private.
Proposal 902 covers part of this too, so I don't think we need a new option.

sources.title: [tor-dev] [Proposal] Weekly guard rotation
passages: From: Tor Project Core Team
As the Tor Project, we propose that clients rotate their entry guards every week.

sources.title: [tor-dev] Re: Building with an older compiler

sources.title: [tor-dev] [TOOL PROPOSAL & PoC] guardscan: a scanner for guard relays
passages: We wrote guardscan, an open-source tool that scans guard relays and onion service directories for configuration problems.
It complements existing exit scanners. The code and our first results are on our website.
